newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Motor reports labour dispute.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Motor reports labour dispute.

text.p: The union of South Korea's largest car maker, Hyundai Motor, said on Wednesday it had notified the labour ministry of a labour dispute.
The notification came after labour and management failed to reach an agreement in their annual wage negotiations.
Union officials said the union demanded a 9.38 percent increase in their basic wages, while the company offered 4.56 percent.
They said more than 80 percent of union members voted for labour action, but Hyundai Motor officials said the percentage was lower than 70 percent.
"We can go on strike any time technically, but decided to delay industrial actions until another wage negotiation on Monday," said Kim Choong-hyun, a union leader.
